page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-48 is an x86_64 server instance provisioned with 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled. It incorporates 384 GB of system memory, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The underlying architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1 data cache, alongside hardware instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring persistent block storage to be attached separately over the network.

Benchmark evaluations position the n4-highmem-48 in the top tier for parallel processing and sustained memory throughput. It demonstrates strong results in the PassMark CPU suite (58,640.65) and Geekbench multi-core testing (16,867.0), reinforced by robust performance in ray tracing, image processing, and hardware-accelerated encryption. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate strong uncached sequential throughput, achieving 254.09 GB/sec for reads and 113.1 GB/sec for writes. Single-thread execution registers in the middle tier across stress-ng and Geekbench single-core workloads.

The primary tradeoff of this instance profile lies in its storage and peripheral architecture. The absence of local NVMe disks means that high-IOPS applications rely entirely on remote network storage volumes, and zero bundled public IPv4 addresses necessitate cloud NAT or dedicated network address allocations. Furthermore, single-thread compute capabilities remain baseline despite the substantial multi-core and vector extensions throughput.

Given its 384 GB memory footprint and high multi-threaded performance, the n4-highmem-48 is structured for large in-memory databases, medium-scale LLM prompt processing, dense web-serving tiers, and heavy multi-threaded analytics that demand large working memory without dedicated GPU hardware.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-48 is a memory-oriented server instance powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel processors, featuring 48 vCPUs, 24 physical cores, and 384 GB of system RAM, providing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Supported by advanced instructions including AVX-512 and AMX, it delivers strong multi-core throughput and high uncached memory bandwidth reaching 254.09 GB/sec read and 113.1 GB/sec write. It carries no local storage or onboard GPUs, relying on networked storage architectures. Benchmark data highlights top-quartile execution in PassMark CPU testing, image manipulation, encryption tasks, and static web serving throughput, while single-core compute performance remains balanced. This configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy enterprise deployments that do not require specialized hardware accelerators, such as in-memory caching layers, medium-scale LLM prompt ingestion, relational database operations, and high-concurrency web services.
